articles.title: Jobe Bellingham called up by England, Sunderland face jeers and the FA Cup first round: football news – live
articles.summary: ⚽ All the latest heading into a busy weekend of football ⚽ Premier League: 10 things to look out for | Mail David. What do we make of that then? Josh King a better player than Cole Palmer? Looks like this goes beyond just playing ability.
body: Jobe Bellingham and Josh King are the headline names after Thomas Tuchel handed both uncapped midfielders call-ups to his England squad for the Nations League games against Croatia and Spain. Borussia Dortmund’s Bellingham, 21, joins his brother Jude in the senior set-up after impressing as captain of the Under-21s.

King’s rise has been just as rapid. The 19-year-old has become a fixture in Fulham’s midfield this season, and his two Premier League goals make him their top league scorer. He travelled with England’s preparation squad before the summer’s World Cup and has kept catching the eye for the Under-21s.
The former Wolves man has called it a day at 33 having featured for Charlton in the second half of the last Championship season. He earned the last of his 10 England caps in 2022.
Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany is on track for a “full recovery” after a lengthy absence following his collapse at a training session, his assistant Aaron Danks has confirmed.

articles.title: Major League Rugby could get Buffalo team amid talks with 17 other locations
articles.summary: Buffalo Thunderbolts would enter league in 2028. League could expand in time for 2031 World Cup. Major League Rugby will play with just five teams in 2027 but has signed a letter of intent with the Buffalo Thunderbolts regarding a bid for entry in 2028 and is in discussions with 17 groups regarding…
body: MLR was formed in 2018, and by 2022 the competition supported 13 teams. In 2025, teams in Utah, Miami, Los Angeles, Houston and New Orleans dropped out.

The league went ahead in 2026 with just six teams but Anthem RC, a World Rugby backed project in Charlotte, North Carolina, will not return next year. Seattle Seawolves, champions in 2018 and 2019, are the only founding members remaining. The other teams are Chicago Hounds, New England Free Jacks, Old Glory DC and California Legion.

MLR co-president Alex Magleby, a former US Eagles flanker and coach, told the Guardian the league hoped six of the 17 groups in talks to host a team would enter a formal bid process ahead of the 2028 season, with three to be selected.

Magleby described a “disciplined, milestone-driven expansion framework,” with candidates advancing “through distinct vetting gates: initial milestone review under a Letter of Intent (LOI), an Exclusive Negotiating Agreement (ENA), and final Board approval before a definitive Franchise Agreement is awarded”.

articles.title: Coach who helped Sinner to the top set to depart
articles.summary: The coach who helped guide Jannik Sinner to five Grand Slam titles and the world number one spot is to leave the player's camp at the end of the year.
body: Australian Darren Cahill, 61, joined the Italian's team in June 2022 when Sinner was just outside the world's top 10 and had never progressed beyond the quarter-finals of a Grand Slam tournament.
But, together with Italian coach Simone Vagnozzi, Cahill has helped Sinner to go on to win five Slams and occupy the world number one spot for 95 weeks.
Injury has meant the 25-year-old has not played since winning Wimbledon for the second year in a row in July, which led to Alexander Zverev recently overtaking him at the top of the rankings.
He is set to return to action at the Six Kings Slam tournament in Saudi Arabia next month.

articles.title: Nottingham Forest’s historic goal drought at home is part of longstanding problem
articles.summary: Oliver Glasner’s side are yet to score at City Ground this season but troubles in front of goal precede his arrival. Nottingham Forest and Schalke are yet to score at home in 2026-27.
body: They also failed to find the net in a Carabao Cup home game with Leeds, meaning they have amassed 70 shots in all competitions without giving the home fans a goal to celebrate. As extreme as this situation has become, Forest scored only two goals more than the lowest home scorers in the Premier League last season (Burnley), drawing a blank on nine occasions. This is a longstanding issue.

The dishonour of scoring the fewest home goals in Europe’s big five leagues in modern times belongs to Dijon, who bagged eight in 19 Ligue 1 games in 2020-21. Fulham went one goal better in the same season to claim the Premier League’s wooden spoon for home scoring. Both scored three across their first four games, showing the unlikely depths to which Forest’s attack has sunk at the City Ground.

With expected goals a frequent element of post-match analysis, it can be easy to overlook that shots are independent of each other. One is not more likely to be converted when those that preceded it were missed, even though the team’s xG total ticks upward. A side that produced one expected goal through 100 shots valued at 0.01 xG would be far from guaranteed to score.
points: Oliver Glasner’s side are yet to score at City Ground this season but troubles in front of goal precede his arrival.

articles.title: Amar Dedic set to escape Newcastle sanction over carrying bow and arrow
articles.summary: Right-back sparked armed police response over incident. Expected to start Newcastle’s trip to Fulham on Saturday. Newcastle’s Amar Dedic is unlikely to face a club sanction after being spotted holding a bow and arrow in the Northumberland countryside and sparking a major police pursuit involving an…
body: Dedic is expected to start Newcastle’s match at Fulham on Saturday following an incident that at one point saw six patrol cars pursue the Bosnia right-back back to his home on the upmarket Darras Hall estate, just outside Ponteland.

Northumbria Police were alerted on Wednesday afternoon when a member of the public spotted Dedic and a friend walking through the Northumberland countryside equipped with bows and arrows. This equipment was eventually seized from the boot of the 24-year-old’s car when he arrived back home at Darras Hall.

In a statement the force said they were satisfied the bows and arrows were “for recreational use and there was no threat to the public”, but inquires were “on-going”. Pursuing animals using bow and arrows or crossbows is illegal in the UK but there are no suggestions that Dedic or his friend were on a hunting expedition.

“Shortly after 1.55pm on Wednesday we received a report of two men carrying a bow and arrow while walking along a track by the reservoir on the Military Road in the Harlow Hill area,” said Northumbria police. “Officers attended and subsequently stopped a vehicle in the Darras Hall area and seized bows and arrows.”

articles.title: Newcastle's Dedic stopped by police after being spotted with bow and arrows
articles.summary: Newcastle United defender Amar Dedic is at the centre of a police investigation after being spotted carrying a bow and arrows at a Northumberland beauty spot.
body: Bosnia-Herzegovina international Dedic, 24, was with a friend when he was stopped in a car after a concerned member of the public raised the alarm.
Reports say six police cars, external were dispatched, including armed police, and that Dedic and his companion were stopped about seven miles away from where they were originally spotted.
Police searched the car and seized the bow and arrows but were satisfied the two men were not a threat to the public.
BBC Sport has been told Dedic had no ill intention and has fully co-operated with police.

articles.title: Moyes talks trophy as Everton boss reflects on career before landmark game
articles.summary: Everton are seventh in the Premier League table with the chance to move above Liverpool into fifth if they can beat Coventry at home. They are also into a Carabao Cup quarter-final against Fleetwood. This has been a promising start for David Moyes.
body: "When you start to talk about quarter-finals, it sounds good," Moyes tells Sky Sports. "Every Evertonian wants a cup run because we have been so long since we have been near lifting any trophies. My expectations are that I want us to be challenging."

There was not huge optimism at the start of the season when Everton sold Iliman Ndiaye and were unable to make the signings they had hoped for late in the transfer window. "We had a difficult summer," concedes Moyes. But it has been a better autumn.

"I think the players have done a great job in getting ourselves into this position." But how about some credit for the manager too? Everton were at a low ebb when he took over last year, but Moyes has more than stabilised, raising the standards at the club again.

Next month, in his second spell alone, he will become Everton's longest-serving manager since Roberto Martinez - the man who first replaced him over 13 years ago. But there is a bigger landmark that he will reach at the Hill Dickinson Stadium on Friday.

articles.title: McIlroy surges into contention at Abu Dhabi Championship
articles.summary: Rory McIlroy stormed into contention at the Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship with a sensational second-round display, carding 11 birdies to reach 11 under par.
body: It was the most birdies McIlroy has ever recorded in a single DP World Tour round. Having started the day on two under par, the two-time Masters champion carded a stunning second-round 63 at Yas Links Golf Club.
Jon Rahm, Tyrrell Hatton and England's Matthew Jordan are also firmly in contention near the top of the leaderboard, although all three are yet to complete their second rounds.
Meanwhile, England's Tommy Fleetwood made a significant move up the standings, carding five consecutive birdies on his front nine before signing for an impressive six-under-par 66.

McIlroy, who is out to leapfrog Race to Dubai Rankings leader Eugenio Chacarra to win a record-equalling eighth Order of Merit title, dropped off the pace on Thursday after he was assessed a two-stroke penalty for improving his lie at the par-4 12th.

body: Joe Coyd (with four) and Rob Hawkins (with three) scored seven of England's 12 tries with Mason Billington and King twice crossing and Jack Brown the other try scorer for the reigning champions at the Wollongong Entertainment Arena.
The result means England head into their last-four meeting with co-hosts Australia on Tuesday (08:45 GMT) with a 100% record, having thrashed Wales and the USA in the group stage.
However, they were far from comfortable against an Ireland side who led 14-0 and 20-4 during the first half before England recovered to take a 22-20 advantage into the break.
"We knew it was going to be a challenge and our biggest in the tournament so far but that is why we are here. We love these high-pressure games," King told Premier Sports.

articles.title: Palmer left out of England squad as Jobe and King called up
articles.summary: Thomas Tuchel has left Cole Palmer out of the England squad, along with Phil Foden and Kobbie Mainoo, but Jude Bellingham’s brother Jobe and Fulham midfielder Josh King have earned their first senior call-ups.
body: Chelsea's Palmer was hugely disappointed when he was overlooked for the World Cup in the summer after a stop-start season due to injury, and he withdrew from the last England camp in September and October because of a minor fitness issue, but he has been back to his best this season with five goals and three assists in 11 appearances.

England made medical checks with Chelsea on Thursday over Palmer and Sky Sports News understands those checks confirmed he was fully fit and ready to take a full part in England's upcoming Nations League matches against Croatia and Spain.

Speaking about Palmer's omission on Friday, Tuchel said the "door is always open" for him and added: "I guess everyone is desperate to play for England, Cole is no exception. It counts when you're in camp. I said last time, he misses too many opportunities to impress. The players who were in camp built something extraordinary.
"It's not personal. We'll never assume Cole isn't in the mindset to come and play for his country but the competition is on and the players in the [last] camp did an amazing job."

articles.title: Australia add Hussey to coaching staff ahead of 2027 Ashes
articles.summary: Australia have brought former batting great Mike Hussey into their coaching setup as they look to address recent batting struggles ahead of next year’s Ashes series in England.
body: The appointment was announced on Friday, with Hussey's stint also taking in the 2027 50-over ‌World Cup in Africa as well as the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics and ​subsequent T20 World Cup later that year.

The Australian Test side, in particular, have faced mounting scrutiny over ​their batting after slumping to a 2-1 series defeat in South Africa in October, having collapsed to 99 all out in the second Test in Gqeberha and 111 all out on the final day of the series-decider in Cape Town.
The setback followed ​a shock nine-wicket loss at home to Bangladesh in August, their first ever in Tests to the Tigers.
"I am extremely excited about being a part of the team in a more formal and meaningful ‌role in the coming years," Hussey said of his appointment in a statement.

body: "I would like to think there is a higher ceiling," says Frank Lampard.

articles.title: Thomas Tuchel explains Cole Palmer omission: ‘He misses too many opportunities’
articles.summary: Thomas Tuchel says he has “enough” No 10s in his England squad without selecting Cole Palmer, who has paid the price for pulling out of the September camp last time out and missing “too many opportunities to impress”.
body: The Chelsea star was a notable omission from Tuchel’s 25-man squad ahead of the Nations League games against Croatia and Spain and he was available for selection. Tuchel criticised Palmer for missing “too many camps with injuries” following his withdrawal from last month’s group and the manager has opted to stick with many of the same players who impressed him last time.

Tuchel has named several No 10s in his group, Morgan Rogers, Morgan Gibbs-White, Eberechi Eze, Jude Bellingham, as well as first-time call-ups Josh King and Jobe Bellingham, who both offer versatility in his midfield.

Palmer has not played for England since March and was missed the World Cup after struggling with injuries last season. He has played in all nine of Chelsea’s Premier League matches this season, but was also sent off in the defeat to Tottenham.

Speaking at a press conference at Wembley, Tuchel explained: “It counts when you are in camp and I just said it last time, he misses too many opportunities to impress. It was a long camp. It was two-and-a-half weeks and the players and the boys who were in camp built something extraordinary throughout these weeks.

articles.title: Balogun Returns To Monaco Squad After Goal And Transfer Drama
articles.summary: U.S. striker Folarin Balogun is back in the lineup for Monaco. He has been added to the squad for the Conference League after scoring his first goal of the season. This move comes after weeks of uncertainty regarding his future with the club.
body: Balogun had been left out of the initial squad list due to pending transfer talks. Now his name appears among the forwards on the official UEFA website, according to Yahoo Sports. His return marks a fresh start after a difficult few months on and off the field. The striker finally found the net in a 3-1 loss to Paris FC on Sunday. He played as a substitute in that match, which was his first goal this season.

The path to this squad addition was rocky. Balogun was very close to joining Everton before the summer transfer window closed. A reported 40 million pounds ($54 million) deal was on the table for the transfer. The move collapsed on the last day of the window, which was Sept. 1 in most European leagues. Balogun pulled out because he felt uncomfortable with how the English club handled his medical exam. Doubts regarding his health were raised by the English club during that checkup. This hesitation cost him a move to a major league and left him with Monaco.
